subject: RealtimeAI: attenuated streaming throughput — mitigation steps & timeline
messages:
From: David Walsh <david.walsh@realtimeai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Realtime: intermittent slow streaming responses this morning

Irene,

We started seeing elevated tail latency for streaming chat responses across our EU and US clusters starting around 08:50 PDT. Clients experience long pauses between chunks (~3-6s) and occasional incomplete streams that require reconnects. This is impacting our live demo traffic and a handful of customer sessions.

Quick facts from our side:
- Observed since ~08:50 PDT
- Affects streaming endpoints only; non-streaming completions appear mostly fine
- Error rate is low, but chunk pacing is poor
- We've tried reconnects and small backoff, which helps briefly

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side, and if there are any quick mitigations we should apply while you triage? We can provide logs and packet captures if helpful.

Thanks,
David Walsh
Engineering Lead, RealtimeAI
ops@realtimeai.com

[attachment: latency-dashboards.png]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: David Walsh <david.walsh@realtimeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: intermittent slow streaming responses this morning

David — thank you for the timely report and the dashboard screenshot. We've engaged the on-call infra team and I wanted to share immediate, actionable mitigations you can try while we investigate root cause: 

Short-term mitigations (can be applied in minutes):
- Switch to the non-streaming completions endpoint for critical demo sessions (reduces chunking overhead).
- Reduce request "max_tokens" from 1024 -> 512 to reduce per-request generation time if acceptable for the use case.
- Enable SDK option "stream_chunk_size": 512 (helps client-side pacing) and increase client-side read timeout to 30s.
- If you see reconnects, set client to resume with the same session id (we're working on a sticky-prefix improvement).
- Use model variant: "redwood-medium-quantized" as a temporary fallback for lower tail-latency.

We are collecting telemetry now. Marissa (SE) is pulling per-route traces and Vivek (Sales/Customer Success) is aligned to keep you updated and prioritize your demo windows. I'll keep this thread updated every 30–45 minutes with findings.

Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0148

[attachment: mitigation-checklist.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: David Walsh <david.walsh@realtimeai.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: intermittent slow streaming responses this morning

Team — quick update from infra:

What we're seeing:
- Two edge shards experienced prolonged GC + kernel contention during a config rollout between 08:40–09:05 PDT, which delayed token emission pacing.
- Autoscaler bounced a small set of GPUs in the affected region while jobs were warm; this increased backend latency for streaming specifically due to KV-cache rehydration delays.

Immediate actions taken by infra:
- Rolled back the config change to stop further bounces.
- Disabled aggressive cache expiry on the affected shards to accelerate KV-cache warmup.
- Enabled temporary routing to healthy regional capacity for new streaming sessions (this will route some US sessions to a warm EU pool while we fully remediate).

Suggested next steps for RealtimeAI (we discussed with David):
1) For demo-critical sessions: route production users to non-streaming endpoints for the next 90 minutes.
2) Apply the SDK tweak Irene mentioned: stream_chunk_size + higher read timeout.
3) If you need continuity, we can enable a targeted sticky routing flag for a subset of sessions (requires approval; I've included the link below).

I'll publish a short postmortem and timeline once infra finishes root cause delta. For now, our priority is to stabilize your demo window.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
"Helping integrations stay live"

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: intermittent slow streaming responses this morning — resolution & follow-up

David — quick resolution summary and next steps: thank you again for the fast report and for trying the SDK adjustments.

What we fixed:
- Root cause: a stage rollout introduced a config that briefly increased cache expiry and caused a small number of edge shards to rehydrate KV caches concurrently while warm GPU nodes were cycling. That combination produced token emission pauses for streaming-only workloads.
- We rolled back the rollout, disabled aggressive expiry, and temporarily routed new streaming sessions to warm pools; these actions brought chunk pacing back to normal by ~11:20 PDT.

Customer impact window: 08:40–11:20 PDT (approximately 2h40m). Impact concentrated on streaming endpoints; non-streaming completions were minimally affected.

Recommended follow-ups for RealtimeAI:
- Keep demo traffic on non-streaming endpoint for the rest of today as a precaution.
- If you need, we can toggle the sticky routing flag for key sessions (we can keep it on for 24 hours).
- We'll share a clean CSV of affected session ids and a postmortem timeline in the next 24 hours.

What we'll deliver from Redwood in 24h:
- Incident timeline and root cause notes (postmortem).
- A targeted SDK snippet that implements graceful reconnect + resume for interrupted streams.
- Offer: one week of expanded support windows for RealtimeAI's demo period to make sure there are no regressions.

Let me know if you'd like a quick 15-min sync; Vivek can join for exec-level context.

Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Irene.Choi@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0148
